request.what: Fund UTxO RPC by TxPipe: Maintaining Cardano's Integration Standard, Year 2, including 12 months of part-time maintenance plus Intersect administration.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve to fund a part-time UTxO RPC maintainer over 12 months at an annual rate of $105,000 USD.
The total requested withdrawal is 540,750 ADA, consisting of 525,000 ADA for UTxO RPC maintenance and enhancement and 15,750 ADA for an Intersect Budget Administration fee.
UTxO RPC is an open interface specification that standardizes interactions with UTxO-based blockchains using Protocol Buffers and SDKs in Rust, Go, Node.js, .NET, Haskell, and Python.
UTxO RPC has been adopted by Amaru, Dingo, and the Haskell Cardano node as a query interface, validating it as a standard across the ecosystem.
The project maintains more than 10 repositories covering the core specification, language-specific SDKs, documentation, and provider integrations under the Apache 2.0 open-source license.
The maintainer scope includes specification maintenance, SDK maintenance, community support, and AI-friendly documentation and integration resources.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain Treasury Withdrawal submission.
The proposer states that the request does not, alone or in aggregate at submission time, breach the 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals from Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 currently under development and on schedule.

Treasury funds would be managed through Intersect using Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, multi-role authorization thresholds, oversight entities, milestone-based disbursement controls, and a public dashboard.

summary: The document asks for 540,750 ADA to continue UTxO RPC maintenance by TxPipe for 12 months through Intersect-administered treasury smart contracts, citing ecosystem adoption, open-source infrastructure value, prior funding history, Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, and oversight mechanisms.
